explanations.answer: Just like what each one sowed
explanations.explanation: You've got the farmer's math, baker. Paul says, "Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously." The harvest follows the seed. Plant a pinch, get a pinch. Plant a LOT, and the field notices.

explanations.answer: The same size for both of them
explanations.explanation: Nice try, friend, but the seed doesn't work that way. Paul says "Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously." So the two harvests are not the same. Each one follows what was sown.

explanations.answer: Bigger for the one who sowed less
explanations.explanation: I love the optimism, friend, but that's like skipping the dough and expecting a full cookie box. Paul says the one who "…sows sparingly will also reap sparingly…" The little sower gets the little harvest. It's the one who sows generously who reaps generously.

Close, but Paul says the opposite. He says each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, "…not out of regret or compulsion." So no arm-twisting and no pressure. The giving comes from the heart.

That's right, baker. Paul says each one should give what he has decided in his heart, "…not out of regret or compulsion." That's his instruction: no pressure and no regret. The choice starts in the heart.
That's the one. Paul says, "For God loves a cheerful giver." Cheerful is the word he picks, friend. That's the kind of giver Paul points to when he says to give from the heart.
Hold on, friend, Paul never says a word about how much is in anybody's pockets. He says, "For God loves a cheerful giver." It's about the heart behind the gift, not the size of the bank account.
I get it, careful sounds responsible. But Paul says, "For God loves a cheerful giver." Careful isn't the word he picks. Cheerful is.

Yes, baker. Paul says God is able to make all grace abound, "…so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work." Notice the all, all, all in there. It's a LOT of all.
Wisdom is wonderful, but it's not what Paul lists here. He says that with all grace and all they need, they "…will abound in every good work." The overflow goes toward good works.
I would love an overflow of rest, believe me. I've napped on a flour sack or two. But Paul says they "…will abound in every good work." The grace is for doing good.

That's right. Paul writes, "He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever." The gifts go to the poor. And Paul says it's "written," so he's leaning on Scripture here.

Ooh, careful, friend! I've been tripped up by easier ones than this, and I live on a cookie planet. Paul writes, "He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever." Those gifts are scattered abroad, and they go to the poor. No trick in this one, so True was the answer.
I see why you'd say it, but Paul says more than that. He says God "…will supply and multiply your store of seed…" Multiply, friend. A store that stays the same size isn't multiplying.

Right on, baker. Paul says God "…will supply and multiply your store of seed and will increase the harvest of your righteousness." The seed store grows, and so does the harvest. Same size is not in this letter.
That's the word. Paul says God "…will increase the harvest of your righteousness." Seed goes in, and a harvest of righteousness comes out. That's the kind of crop Paul has in mind.
I know, a bigger savings account sounds lovely. But Paul never says that here. He says God "…will increase the harvest of your righteousness." The harvest he names is righteousness.
A good reputation is nice, but it's not the crop Paul names. He says God "…will increase the harvest of your righteousness." Righteousness is the word in the verse, friend.
You got it, baker. Paul says "…through us your generosity will produce thanksgiving to God." The generosity goes out, and the thanks go up to God.

Sacrifices is a fair guess, friend, and I've grabbed the wrong word off the shelf plenty of times myself. But it isn't in this verse. Paul says "…through us your generosity will produce thanksgiving to God." The generosity goes out, and what it produces is thanksgiving.

Tithes are a fair guess, since we're talking about giving. But Paul doesn't use the word here. He says "…through us your generosity will produce thanksgiving to God." The result is thanksgiving, friend.

That's it. Paul says the saints "…will glorify God for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ, and for the generosity of your contribution…" So the gift proves something. It shows an obedient confession of the gospel.
Teaching is a good gift, but Paul doesn't mention it here. He says the saints will glorify God "…for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ…" So it's their obedience to the gospel.

explanations.answer: Their good name in the city
explanations.explanation: I got my name carved on a handle, so I know names matter to people. But Paul doesn't say this one. The saints will glorify God "…for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ…" That's the other thing they glorify God for.
